notes:
I couldn't do this research. My one attempt to fetch the sources was cut off by the tool's usage limit, and I wasn't able to make any more calls, so I never read a single page.

You asked for notes based only on what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point. Since I have no source content, I'm not giving you any notes. Anything I wrote now would come from my own memory, not from cited sources.

**Pages I was going to read first:**
- Enduring Word (Guzik): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-3/
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/3.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/ezekiel/3.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/ezekiel/3.htm
- Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel-3-commentary
- Wesley's Notes (Methodist): https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-ezekiel/

**Where I'd expect traditions to differ (to check against the sources):**
- **Vv. 20–21**, the righteous man who turns away and dies. This is where Reformed and Baptist readers (who hold that true believers can't finally fall away) are likely to split from Wesleyan and Methodist readers (who hold they can). I'd look at Ligonier, GTY, Desiring God, Seedbed and Wesley.
- **Vv. 17–19**, the watchman. This passage is often used as a model for pastors and for evangelism. I'd check Got Questions, The Gospel Coalition and Spurgeon. On the Catholic side, Gregory the Great's *Pastoral Rule* on New Advent may cite these verses.
- **Vv. 1–3 and 25–27**, eating the scroll and Ezekiel's silence. For modern scholarly views, I'd check the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey.

If you ask again in a new message, I can start from these pages and write the verse-by-verse notes, citing only what each page says.
